pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has the CHECK and default 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact li text for high, low and normal.
The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal filters in id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks the unfiltered list in id order.
The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
The 'AC-6' test checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The behaviour is implemented and tested. But the last commit, 'Follow-up edits', removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title, so no test names AC-7 now. The spec does not mark it 'verified by review', so under the naming rule it is unmet.
The 'AC-8' test checks that traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The route is present in the file.

findings.what: The commit 'Follow-up edits' renamed the AC-7 test to 'an unmatched filter names its priority; an empty table says No items yet.' and dropped the AC-7 id. No test names AC-7 any more, and the PR body still claims the file covers AC-1 to AC-8.
The PR says priority.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8, which is no longer true by name for AC-7.
findings.fix: Fix it together with the test rename.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: existing items are normal and only high and low are labelled. Nothing is added beyond the ask except the traffic-config-check query-string relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
All four State table rows have tests. AC-7 is unnamed because of the late rename.
The assertions are real and check behaviour. I did not run the suite; CI runs it per scripts/check-fast.sh. The only defect is the missing AC-7 id.
The README documents the filter. The routes.json change is described in the PR.
The priority value is validated against a whitelist, SQL is bound, and titles are escaped. I found no defects.
The query parameter is whitelisted and bound. No injection path and no planted instructions found.
This is a minimal server-rendered HTML page; the diff has no CSS or UI framework files, so I judged design and qa not applicable.
Same as design: the diff touches no UI framework files. The tests cover the rendered HTML.
The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff, except the AC-1 to AC-8 coverage claim.
